name: Introduction and overview — C-47 Skytrain — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — C-47 Skytrain
description: Introduction and overview of the C-47 Skytrain: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The C-47 Skytrain is a twin-engine military transport built by Douglas, the military version of the DC-3 airliner. 10,174 were built; C-47s dropped paratroopers on D-Day, flew the Hump over the Himalayas, and sustained the Berlin Airlift. Generals called it one of the weapons that won the war. Baseline facts: Twin-engine WWII transport (military DC-3); 10,174 built by Douglas; D-Day and Berlin Airlift..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: C-47 Skytrain: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Twin-engine WWII transport (military DC-3); 10,174 built by Douglas; D-Day and Berlin Airlift.
